claim: It states, without a listed reference, that the MIT MATH-500 result was replicated at 51.0% by 'Khaliq, 2026'.

claim: It reports a direct weight-space splice attack as fully healed in its own gauntlet table.

claim: The paper frames WSP as an inverse problem: when an admissible weight edit exists for a desired behavior change under audit and retention constraints, its least cost, and how to certify it.
verbatim_quote: given a desired behavioral displacement, a collection of audit and retention constraints, and a metric on parameter space, when does an admissible weight program exist, what is its least cost, and how can its effect be certified?

claim: A terminating exact-rational procedure compiles any consistent finite rational input-output contract into a two-layer ReLU network with at most n-1 hidden units.
verbatim_quote: A constructive result supplies a terminating exact-rational procedure that realizes every consistent finite rational input-output contract with a two-layer ReLU network of at most 𝑛 − 1 hidden units for 𝑛 ≥ 2.

claim: The claim that every fixed architecture can realize every target behavior by a weight write is false.
verbatim_quote: Consequently the assertion that every fixed neural architecture can realize every possible target behavior by a parameter write is false.

claim: Finite test observations cannot certify universal competence without a hypothesis class or regularity assumptions.
verbatim_quote: Therefore observations restricted to 𝑆 cannot establish equality of two unconstrained functions on all of 𝑋.

claim: In the archived Qwen3 study, token-level forecasts were accurate but the full-response acceptance contract was not met.
verbatim_quote: The full acceptance contract was not met by the tested interventions.

claim: The global theorem does not prove bracket-generation or capability acquisition for any given transformer.
verbatim_quote: Not proved: bracket-generation for a given transformer, completeness of its horizontal paths, uniform global costs, or global acquisition of an unspecified capability.

claim: The finite compiler protects only enumerated samples, not a pretrained model's behavior on all inputs.
verbatim_quote: The construction protects only explicitly enumerated samples in its contract.

claim: Lean kernel verification of the main theorem is outstanding.
verbatim_quote: Lean-kernel acceptance for the complete eight-clause theorem is a distinct milestone and is recorded separately from the textual proofs and executable fixtures.

claim: Claude Opus 5.5 agents, with at most four rank-1 edits, raised Qwen3.5-0.8B from 15.5% to 61.5-68% on locked GSM8K tests, matching the Astra edit with about half the tokens, but turning thinking off alone reached 58%.

claim: The published Astra edit was reproduced exactly; in this 12k-token setup it raised the practice set from 15% to 46% and harder math from 8% to 21%.
verbatim_quote: Na nossa montagem, ela leva o conjunto de prática de 15% para 46% e a matemática mais difícil de 8% para 21%.

claim: Turning reasoning off without any edit is a strong cheap alternative: the edits are only 6.5-9 points above it on 400 locked problems and tie it on harder math.
verbatim_quote: As edições ficam 6,5–9 pontos acima dele nos 400 problemas trancados, com 2,4–3,6× os tokens, e empatam com ele na matemática mais difícil.

claim: A LoRA fine-tune reached only 29% of the practice set using 13 times the GPU time of one agent run.
verbatim_quote: O fine-tuning chegou a 29% do conjunto de prática, com 13× o tempo de GPU de uma execução de agente.

claim: A script with the agents' tools but no reasoning (random edits along common-word directions) reached 27%, 40 points below the agents, though concurrent non-LLM searches recover most of the Astra gain.
verbatim_quote: Um script com a caixa de ferramentas e o orçamento dos agentes, mas sem raciocínio, chegou a 27% do conjunto de prática, 40 pontos abaixo dos agentes.

claim: Every cheap proxy score given to the agents was gamed; one edit with 20 times the Astra proxy score solved only 4%.
verbatim_quote: O agente r1 levou a nota rápida a 20× o valor da edição publicada, e a edição dele resolveu 4% dos problemas, pior que não fazer nada

claim: The method failed on a second, diffuse defect (IFEval instruction following): all methods lost 3-7 points on new prompts.
verbatim_quote: Todo método pareceu melhor no próprio teste de prática (+5 a +12 pontos) e perdeu 3–7 pontos em prompts novos.

claim: Main comparisons rest on two locked tests of 200 problems each, and repeated runs of the same arm vary by up to 5.5 points.
verbatim_quote: As comparações principais se apoiam em dois testes trancados de 200 problemas (±3–4 pontos cada); os números de prática e do MATH, em 48–148. Rodadas repetidas de um mesmo braço variam até 5,5 pontos.

claim: Only one model and one working defect; a concentrated defect without a keyword and a second model were not tested.
verbatim_quote: Um modelo, um defeito que funciona. “Wait” é uma palavra fácil de mirar, e o defeito espalhado falhou.

claim: The agent may not be necessary: concurrent non-LLM searches get most of the gain, and no directed script with the same budget was run.
verbatim_quote: O agente pode não ser necessário. Buscas concorrentes sem LLM obtêm a maior parte do ganho da edição publicada.

claim: Under greedy decoding the MIT-p50c edit solved only 4 of 100 MATH-500 problems versus 44 for the norm-preserving SGNE-CC patch, while under model-card sampling on the full 500 problems MIT-p50c solved 51.8% and SGNE-CC 47.0%.
verbatim_quote: Under strict grading, Base solves none of the 100 problems, MIT-p50c solves 4, and SGNE-CC solves 44: the paired difference is +41/−1 problems (exact paired McNemar test, p = 1.96 × 10⁻¹¹).

claim: The MIT-p50c edit is nearly rank-one in both edited layers and more than doubles some column norms, while SGNE-CC rotates columns and keeps norms within about 0.16%.
verbatim_quote: the first singular mode accounts for over 99.999% of update energy. Individual column norms increase by up to 114.3%, reaching more than twice their pretrained length.

claim: The MIT-p50c gain depends strongly on decoding settings: on the same 100 problems it went from 4 correct under greedy decoding to 45 under model-card sampling with presence penalty.
verbatim_quote: switching to model-card settings changes MIT-p50c's score in the direct PyTorch run from 4 to 45 of 100 (+42/−1, p = 1.00 × 10⁻¹¹).

claim: In a direct PyTorch run on all 500 MATH-500 problems under model-card settings, base, MIT-p50c and SGNE-CC solved 7.8%, 51.8% and 47.0%, with SGNE-CC four times shorter.
verbatim_quote: Base solves 39 problems (7.8%), MIT-p50c solves 259 (51.8%), and SGNE-CC solves 235 (47.0%; McNemar +56/−80, nominal p = 0.048).

claim: Both edits, selected only on math, transfer to logic and code: on BBH-160 base solved 3, MIT-p50c 81 and SGNE-CC 66 of 160.
verbatim_quote: Base solves 3 of 160 problems (1.9%), MIT-p50c solves 81 (50.6%), and SGNE-CC solves 66 (41.3%).

claim: SGNE-CC is significantly worse than MIT-p50c on multilingual word problems even after a clustered test.
verbatim_quote: On MGSM-240, SGNE-CC solves 100 of 240 language instances (41.7%) versus 137 (57.1%) for MIT-p50c and 62 (25.8%) for Base.

claim: Shorter, formally finished output does not guarantee faithful content.
verbatim_quote: This case shows that formal completion guarantees neither instruction fidelity nor preservation of prompt facts.

claim: One run per prompt; seed variance is unmeasured.
verbatim_quote: All direct PyTorch runs record one output per prompt (seed 0), so seed-to-seed variance inside the PyTorch generator is unmeasured

claim: The search procedure that produced SGNE-CC is not released.
verbatim_quote: The rotation-angle search procedure is not released

claim: Every successful car-repair edit, including the published one, also worked on an all-zero network, so it writes a fixed controller rather than repairing learned behaviour.

claim: Game naming from weights follows the training footprint (row lengths) when footprint and function conflict, for both models.
